title: Tamils of the World Will Never Agree!
translatorNote: This translation is intended to carry Kalaignar's voice into clear, contemporary English rather than recast the letter as literary or academic prose. It preserves the source's argument, political directness, rhetorical questions, repetition, irony, factual detail, and paragraph order. Names, dates, figures, quotations, and intentional English expressions are retained. Where Tamil idiom cannot be reproduced literally without sounding unnatural, the English follows its sense and rhetorical force without adding claims absent from the source. The original Tamil is reproduced in full below the translation and remains the authoritative text. `Udanpirappē` is retained in Tamil transliteration rather than flattened into “brother,” “sister,” or “comrade.” Literally evoking “one born alongside me,” Kalaignar uses it as a distinctive address of shared identity, equality, affection, and solidarity within the movement. Letter-specific notes: 1. This letter responds to contemporary political accusations immediately after the DMK's announced withdrawal from the Union Cabinet and the UPA. All descriptions of motives, “betrayal,” “deceptive drama,” war responsibility and political inconsistency remain Kalaignar's attributed argument. 2. The 2009 chronology is preserved as presented in the source, including the account of the Sri Lankan ceasefire announcement and the reasons given for ending Kalaignar's fast; no external chronology is substituted. 3. Names such as **Miliband** and **Kouchner** follow the persons indicated by the Tamil source without adding biographical explanation. 4. `நீலிக்கண்ணீர்` is rendered **crocodile tears**, carrying the source's accusation of insincere grief rather than preserving the literal folk image.
paragraphs: The draft resolution brought by the United States before the U.N. Human Rights Council has been amended four times and diluted to a great extent. The Government of India did not give even the slightest consideration to any of the amendments proposed by the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam. Therefore the DMK decided and announced that it would immediately withdraw from the Union Cabinet and from the United Progressive Alliance. Thousands upon thousands of Udanpirappus like you, and people from many sections, have widely welcomed the DMK's decision as the appropriate decision taken at the right time.

From the day in 1956 when, at the DMK General Council meeting in Chidambaram under Arignar Anna's leadership, I moved a resolution on the Eelam Tamil issue and Ponnambalanar seconded it, right up to today, we have continuously raised our voice without interruption for the welfare and rights of the Eelam Tamils. Eelam Tamils and their leaders knew this well then and know it well today.

I am one who not only lost government twice, in 1976 and 1991, for the Eelam Tamils, but also resigned my seat as a Member of the Legislative Assembly together with Perasiriyar. Whenever Eelam Tamils were harmed, it was the DMK that became alarmed and raised the first voice. For their protection we have conducted every form of moral and peaceful democratic struggle permitted by democracy—marches, public meetings, conference resolutions, human chains, strikes, the creation of TESO and its reconstitution.

Even at today's press conference—19 March 2013—when I was asked, “It is alleged that you did nothing when the war took place in Sri Lanka in 2009?” I replied, “What did we not do in 2009? We were not silent then.”

On 28 March 2009 I wrote to the Prime Minister and Mrs. Sonia Gandhi asking India to help secure an immediate ceasefire in Sri Lanka. In her long reply to me dated 31 March 2009, Mrs. Sonia Gandhi gave a firm assurance: “As a first step there must be a ceasefire in Sri Lanka. Our government is in contact with the Sri Lankan government regarding a ceasefire.” Even after the Government of India asked for the war to stop, Sri Lankan President Rajapaksa did not stop it.

On 7 April 2009 I sent an urgent telegram to Prime Minister Manmohan Singh, Mrs. Sonia Gandhi, External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee and Home Minister P. Chidambaram asking them to save the entire Tamil people in Sri Lanka from being destroyed en masse and to ensure a ceasefire.

During the final war, even after countries such as the United States, Britain, Japan and Norway, and U.N. Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon, appealed to Rajapaksa to protect the Sri Lankan Tamils, what surged instead, the letter argues, was Rajapaksa's Sinhala-majoritarianism and his determination to destroy the Tamil people.
On 9 April 2009 a huge march was held in Chennai under my leadership with the slogan “Sri Lankan government, stop the war!” Sri Lankan President Rajapaksa announced a “two-day ceasefire.”

Accepting my call for a one-day strike on 23 April 2009, Tamil Nadu observed the strike peacefully and successfully. On 24 April Home Minister P. Chidambaram met me and explained developments. The Prime Minister too spoke to me by telephone and described all the steps taken by the Union Government.

On 25 April 2009 a statement was issued on behalf of U.S. President Obama saying that the Sri Lankan government should immediately stop its military offensive. On 27 April, when no news of the kind I had hoped for arrived and the Sri Lankan government had not stopped the war, I went at dawn to the Anna memorial and began a fast even though I had undergone surgery in the region of my side.

At about 11 a.m. that day Sri Lanka's Security Council met, and at around noon the Sri Lankan government issued a statement saying “the war in northern Sri Lanka has come to an end.” On the basis of that statement, Union External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee issued a statement saying “combat operations have ended,” sent a copy to the place where I was fasting, and the Prime Minister and Mrs. Sonia Gandhi asked me to end the fast.

The countries of the world believed the Rajapaksa government's statement that the war had ended. The Union Government believed it and gave me confidence in it as well. The U.S. government itself believed it: U.S. government spokesperson Robert Wood welcomed the Sri Lankan government's ceasefire announcement. On the basis of the Union Government's request, and because leaders and friends from all parties urged me, I ended my fast.

After, during the final war, I had risked my life and undertaken this whole chain of actions through the DMK to protect the Eelam Tamils and bring the war to an end, those who have from the beginning made a habit of finding fault with the DMK and with me—people who have never themselves come forward to sacrifice anything for the Eelam Tamils—continue, even after explanations have been given many times, to repeat the same accusations. That is due to permanent hostility and a malicious desire to divert attention, nothing else. It is their deceptive drama.

After the destruction of the Twin Towers in the United States on 11 September 2001, many countries forgot the distinction between liberation fighters and terrorists, and many countries therefore banned the Tigers organisation. Even representatives of major powers such as British Foreign Secretary Miliband and French Foreign Minister Kouchner tried to find a solution to the Eelam issue and were unable to do so. Some people here may conceal these things, but history will not forget them.

Yet out of political hostility Jayalalithaa has issued a long statement calling the decision announced by the DMK today a deceptive drama. She says that I took no action during the height of the war in Sri Lanka in 2009; that I failed to act on the resolution she brought in the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly; that when the United States brought a resolution before the U.N. Human Rights Council last year I said nothing about it; that instead of calling for a resolution in the Human Rights Council I called for one in the Indian Parliament; and she writes as though I did absolutely nothing on the Eelam Tamil issue while she herself took a special incarnation for their sake.
Neutral observers know well how far the claims in Jayalalithaa's statement are from the truth.

Not only on the Eelam Tamil issue but on many matters affecting the overall welfare of Tamils, Jayalalithaa, the letter charges, has played a double role and staged deceptive dramas. On Arignar Anna's dream, the Sethu Samudram project, and on the Cauvery issue, she has made mutually contradictory statements and supplied the very grammar of what a deceptive political drama looks like.

On the Eelam Tamil issue, during the AIADMK government, a resolution was passed in the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly on 16 April 2002 demanding that the Union Government take immediate steps to have the Sri Lankan government arrest Liberation Tigers leader Velupillai Prabhakaran and hand him over to India; and further urging that, with the Sri Lankan government's permission, the Indian Army be sent to assist Sri Lanka and make the necessary effort to capture Prabhakaran. Jayalalithaa thereby presented herself to the world as an absolute enemy of Velupillai Prabhakaran and the Liberation Tigers.
Jayalalithaa shocked the world, the letter says, by falsely asserting: “The war being waged by Rajapaksa is not against Tamils; it is only against the Liberation Tigers.”
On 17 January 2009 she issued a statement saying:
“The Sri Lankan Army does not intend to kill Sri Lankan Tamils. When a war—a battle—is taking place, it is only natural that innocent people are killed.”

The letter says she thereby justified the Rajapaksa government's bombing that killed innocent Tamils in large numbers and acted as an advocate for the Sri Lankan military. Now, by using the police to suppress the spontaneous mass uprising of students in Tamil Nadu, Jayalalithaa has once again revealed, in the writer's view, her attitude toward the Eelam Tamils. The tears she sheds for them are therefore crocodile tears; what Jayalalithaa stages is a drama, and specifically a deceptive drama.

Just as her approach to the Eelam Tamil issue has been contradictory, she has also, the letter argues, spoken in mutually contradictory ways and staged a deceptive drama over the Sethu Samudram project meant for the progress of the southern districts.

In the AIADMK election manifesto Jayalalithaa issued in 2001, it said that the principal objective of the Sethu Samudram project was to remove the sandbanks and rocks obstructing shipping in the Adam's Bridge area between Rameswaram and Talaimannar in Sri Lanka, deepen the passage and form a canal. In the 2004 manifesto she said the AIADMK would press for sufficient funds to be allocated immediately and for the project to be completed within a specified time frame. What kind of contradiction—what sort of deceptive drama—is it for Jayalalithaa now to demand that Ram Setu be declared a national monument?

On the Cauvery issue too, regarded as fundamental to the livelihood of people in the Delta districts and especially farmers, Jayalalithaa has adopted differing positions. When the Cauvery Authority was constituted under Prime Minister Vajpayee, she disparaged it as a “toothless authority” and a “non-functioning authority.” She even said she had no confidence in Prime Minister Vajpayee as Chairman of the Cauvery Authority and thereby attracted the Supreme Court's condemnation.

When the Cauvery Tribunal's final award was delivered, on 6 February 2007 she angrily declared that it had gone against Tamil Nadu only because of Karunanidhi's continuing acts of betrayal. Yet when that very “adverse award” was published in the Central Gazette, she called it the greatest victory of her thirty-year political life, received the title “Ponniyin Selvi,” and rejoiced. On the Cauvery issue too, the writer says, this is the same deceptive drama.

Jayalalithaa, has she forgotten—or is she trying to hide behind a curtain—the fact that it was because of the continuous pressure applied by the DMK that the Government of India supported the U.S. resolution before the U.N. Human Rights Council last year; our present position that Parliament should adopt the amendments we seek and India should support the American resolution together with those amendments; the enormous response among the people of Tamil Nadu and among students to the TESO conference, its resolutions, demonstrations and strike; and my earlier appeal that whoever raises a voice, from whatever side, for the welfare of the Eelam Tamils should be welcomed, that differing voices must not harm their welfare, and that despite our many differences we should forget them and speak with one voice for the Eelam Tamils?

In order to conceal, the letter charges, the betrayals Jayalalithaa committed against Prime Minister Vajpayee, my dear friend M.G.R. and Mrs. Janaki; the betrayals she committed against Velupillai Prabhakaran and the Liberation Tigers; and the betrayals she continues to commit against the people of Tamil Nadu because of selfish politics, she cries “betrayal, betrayal” at others. Tamils here and Eelam Tamils will not accept that tactic. Tamils around the world will never agree!
With affection, M.K. 21 March 2013
